executionPlan: Measured first and then fixed the real cause. Mask: Body_Mesh and look_0 triangles under the shirt are dropped via normal-ray tests in bind pose. Debug counts showed Body_Mesh loses 0 triangles, so the mask is not the cause. Flat-colour shirt test (no dots) plus a dump of the shirt atlas showed the cause: white islands on BLACK padding, sampled at seams. Final fix: game-only front-face shirt material copy with a dilated-padding texture, weak polygon offset, and a game-only index-reduced geometry clone for pants. Verified by headless Chrome over CDP, a restore probe, unit tests, lint, test and a build in a scratch copy.
summary: Root cause of the dark specks, seam flecks and jagged edges is the shirt texture atlas: black padding gets sampled at UV seams. The thin neck line was the shirt's strong polygon-offset bias (-4/-5000) pulling collar texels over the neck skin. Fix is in game-only code: a padded-texture, front-face shirt material copy, weaker offsets (shirt -1/-500, pants -0.5/-250), and the bind-pose triangle mask applied to a geometry clone. After screenshots (3 views x idle/walk/run) are clean at the torso. The hero is bit-identical after Exit (same material, geometry and texture uuids). Remaining: a very faint light vertical edge on the lower side in one side-idle frame, and fall pose not separately captured.

Hero call (not made) in components/avatar/Avatar.tsx: useEffect(() => { scene.traverse(o => (o as THREE.SkinnedMesh).isSkinnedMesh && (o as THREE.SkinnedMesh).skeleton.pose()); return applyAvatarLook(scene); }, [scene]). The pose call is needed so the mask is computed in bind pose. Expected effect: same clean shirt as in game; the hero would otherwise show the same black seam specks, the neck line and the sleeve flecks. Caveat: the shared mask cache is keyed on the shared geometry, the hero would see the reduced pants index, and the shirt material copy replaces the shared material while mounted.

assumptions: Shared textures and materials stay owned by useGLTF; the game only creates and disposes its own copies.
Software GL (SwiftShader) screenshots are visual evidence only, not performance evidence.
decisionsProposed: The shirt's dark specks came from black atlas padding. Fix at the material level (padded texture copy) rather than with depth bias or triangle masks.
lessonsProposed: Before choosing a fix for rendering specks, rule out texture content: render the mesh with a flat-colour material and dump the map image. If the flat render is clean, the cause is texels and not geometry.
A strong polygon offset on one layer paints it over nearby skin (the neck line). Keep layering biases weak, and use a diagnostic matrix toggling bias before shipping.
Geometry masks need data from the actual mesh. Count the dropped triangles before relying on the mechanism (Body_Mesh dropped zero here).
